charts.title: Fed, ECB and BOJ harmonized policy rates
charts.rationale: Daily BIS harmonized rates on a common axis; compare level and tightening cycles.
charts.caveats: BIS can splice instruments; rate corridor midpoints are not Fed upper bound.

charts.title: Global real GDP growth
charts.rationale: Compare annual constant-price real GDP growth across countries and the world.
charts.caveats: Country composition and revised annual data; avoid projecting onto daily dates.

charts.title: Domestic listed-capitalization to GDP
charts.rationale: Compare listed equity capitalization relative to domestic output.
charts.caveats: Neither series is a perfect Buffett indicator; gaps and listing residence affect ratios.

charts.title: Fed target upper bound versus ECB deposit facility
charts.rationale: Contrast different policy instruments while retaining explicit labels.
charts.caveats: Different monetary-policy instruments; do not call this harmonized policy.

charts.title: CAPE versus 10-year real yield
charts.rationale: Examine whether changing discount rates accompany valuation changes.
charts.caveats: One valuation series is not yet mapped; incompatible units require explicit normalization.

charts.title: Labour share and global listed profits
charts.rationale: Test capture of economic output by labour and listed companies.
charts.caveats: Measures have different coverage; source and definition unresolved.

charts.title: US Sahm Rule and private credit stress
charts.rationale: Examine labour deterioration alongside financial leverage.
charts.caveats: Different frequencies and countries; meaningful alignment remains unspecified.

charts.title: Concentration versus global valuation
charts.rationale: Study how concentrated global equity exposure relates to valuation.
charts.caveats: Both historical datasets require licensing and methodological decisions.

charts.title: Gold versus real yields
charts.rationale: Compare gold movements with inflation-indexed bond yields.
charts.caveats: Monthly gold average versus daily real yield requires explicit frequency alignment and dual-axis display; indexed-to-100 does not work for negative real yields.

charts.title: Public debt versus policy rates
charts.rationale: Compare long-term debt burdens and monetary policy.
charts.caveats: Country aggregation and mixing daily/annual measurements are unresolved.

charts.title: BIS credit-to-GDP gaps — United States, euro area and Japan
charts.rationale: Compare credit booms and deleveraging using the same BIS one-sided HP methodology across geographies.
charts.caveats: Percentage-point gap of private nonfinancial-sector credit to GDP; cross-country comparability depends on statistical definitions and coverage; not a world gap.

charts.title: World productivity growth and labour income share
charts.rationale: Compare changes in global output per worker with workers' share of worldwide income, using two separately-labelled percentage measurements.
charts.caveats: Productivity is an annual growth rate and labour share is a level of income; levels are not directly comparable even though both use percentages. This does not constitute a wage/productivity-gap series.

charts.title: US corporate equities/net worth and Shiller CAPE
charts.rationale: Compare US equities/net worth valuation to earnings-adjusted equity prices, preserving both original measures.
charts.caveats: NCBCEPNW is equity market value versus net worth, not Tobin Q; quarterly versus monthly frequencies and unlike units require explicit alignment and normalization.

charts.title: Monthly gold / MSCI ACWI net-return correlation
charts.rationale: Trace variation in the trailing historical 36-month gold-global-equity return relationship using an actual NETR benchmark.
charts.caveats: World Bank gold monthly mean and monthly mean MSCI ACWI NETR USD index levels; Pearson on consecutive monthly arithmetic returns. Different from the existing GLD/VT ETF proxy.

charts.title: GDP-weighted international private-credit cycle (43 BIS economies)
charts.rationale: Compare country credit-to-GDP deviations using prior-year nominal GDP weights to reflect global credit-cycle exposure.
charts.caveats: Derived GDP-weighted average of national BIS one-sided HP-filter gaps; not an official world/BIS aggregate. Up to 43 economies; threshold >=80% of world GDP; use companion coverage chart.

charts.title: GDP coverage of the international private-credit composite
charts.rationale: Expose quarterly world GDP share represented by economies contributing to the GDP-weighted credit gap.
charts.caveats: Prior calendar-year USD GDP denominator; 80% inclusion threshold. Covered economies and weights vary over time; values below threshold omitted.

charts.title: World listed-company market capitalization relative to world GDP
charts.rationale: Track worldwide listed domestic equity market size relative to nominal global economic output since WDI WFE source history begins.
charts.caveats: Uses WDI WLD listed-market-capitalization / WDI WLD GDP; capital-market country coverage is incomplete and changes through time. Not the WDI country-weighted aggregate CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS.

charts.title: World listed-company capitalization in current US dollars
charts.rationale: Show WFE-sourced WDI world aggregate listed domestic equity capitalization in annual nominal USD.
charts.caveats: USD values and geographic coverage vary; not inflation-adjusted and not the full worldwide listed corporate earnings numerator.

charts.title: Global equities aggregate trailing P/E (Siblis)
charts.rationale: Follow the normalized aggregate index price-to-earnings multiple on officially published month-end snapshots.
charts.caveats: Sparse selected dates rather than a complete historical monthly series; Siblis index covers ~3,000 companies and is not all worldwide listed issuers. Proprietary source; no public redistribution without rights.

charts.title: Global equities normalized trailing earnings yield
charts.rationale: Measure the inverse of the globally published Siblis index P/E as earnings relative to that index's capitalization.
charts.caveats: Not corporate net profits as a share of global GDP. Sparse year-end snapshots and distinct index universe; proprietary data require separate publishing permission.
